issue_context.title: Disabling DNSSEC per link does not work (systemd-resolved)
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 250.4-2

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->
<!--           If there have been multiple stable releases for that major version, please consider updating to a recent one before reporting an issue. -->
<!--           When using a distro package, please make sure that the version reported is meaningful for upstream. -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd-stable/tags for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > archlinux

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `5.17.5-zen1`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x64

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 DNS validation failed on links without DNSSEC validation enabled.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 1. Using `DNSSEC=yes` as a default: everything works.
 2. Setting up a new link with a specific search domain (e.g. ~dummy.com) and another DNS IP
 3. Disable DNSSEC on the new link (DNS server is not compatible)
 4. `resolve query test.dummy.com`: `test.dummy.com: resolve call failed: DNSSEC validation failed: incompatible-server`

Note: this exact same process with DNS-over-TLS works as expected: when disabling DNS/TLS on a specific link, it does actually disable it.

When disabling DNSSEC entirely, everything works.

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

resolvectl output:
<!-- Please paste relevant program terminal or journal output here, ideally
     when generated in debug mode (try setting the SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
     environment variable). For very long copy/pasted data consider using a
     service like https://gist.github.com/. Where copy/paste is not possible
     (for example early boot or late shutdown), a photo of the screen might do
     too, but text is always much preferred. -->
```text
Global
           Protocols: -LLMNR +mDNS +DNSOverTLS DNSSEC=yes/supported
    resolv.conf mode: stub
  Current DNS Server: 9.9.9.9#dns.quad9.net
         DNS Servers: 9.9.9.9#dns.quad9.net 149.112.112.112#dns.quad9.net 2620:fe::fe#dns.quad9.net 2620:fe::9#dns.quad9.net
Fallback DNS Servers: 1.1.1.1#cloudflare-dns.com 9.9.9.9#dns.quad9.net 8.8.8.8#dns.google 2606:4700:4700::1111#cloudflare-dns.com 2620:fe::9#dns.quad9.net
                      2001:4860:4860::8888#dns.google
          DNS Domain: ~.

Link 14 (geeTest)
    Current Scopes: DNS
         Protocols: +DefaultRoute +LLMNR -mDNS -DNSOverTLS DNSSEC=no/unsupported
Current DNS Server: 172.30.0.2
       DNS Servers: 172.30.0.2
        DNS Domain: ~. ~dummy.com

```

review_comments: Same here, why not call `link_allocate_scopes()` in `link_set_dnssec_mode()`?
`link_set_dns_over_tls_mode()` is called on sd-network change, and in that case, `link_allocate_scope()` will be called after all sd-network properties are parsed.
